from neighboring configurations or repository history.

The wake-visual skill is applicable because it explicitly governs multi-wake policy changes. Its workspace-relative shortcut isn’t present here, so I’m loading the exact installed skill path, then I’ll follow its prescribed keyframe-first evidence order.

The scalar evidence separates three regimes: the assigned parent reaches only 53.2% progress, a near miss reaches 70.9% but bottoms out at 3.25L, and the strongest sampled policy reaches the 0.75L capture at 266.3 time units. I’m now comparing their keyframe sheets—starting with the shared prewarm—so the policy change is tied to trajectory topology, not score alone.

The visual comparison points to a narrow, evidence-backed exploit rather than a new feedback mechanism. The parent’s 19° gait self-propels and corrects laterally but stops 5.81L short; the isolated 20°/0.67 change reaches the target with lower force/moment and lower mean power than the 21°/0.69 softened-steering near miss, which rebounds from 3.25L to 3.61L. I’m recording that diagnosis before implementing the sampled successful architecture as the single candidate.

The candidate and both required evidence files are now updated. I’m moving to the mandated checker and lightweight contract validation only; I will not run the formal CFD rollout, which remains EvE’s post-exit evaluation.
